meta.summary: A seed packet that's spent a week on the kitchen counter: warm cream paper, soil-brown text, faded green ink for the stamp and headings, and tomato red only where something needs noticing. Fonts (Rubik, Atkinson Hyperlegible, Caveat) approved by Scott 2026-11-03.

concept: A seed packet that's spent a week on the kitchen counter. Warm paper, faded green ink, and a little red where you need to notice something.

cream.name: Seed-packet cream
cream.role: Main background for posts, labels, inserts and the site.
cream.rule: Cream does most of the work. Aim for cream on roughly two thirds of every post, because the brand reads as paper first.

soil.name: Potting-soil brown
soil.role: Body copy, planting instructions, small type.
soil.rule: All body copy and instructions are soil brown. It is the only palette color that passes small-text contrast on cream (11.5:1).

pea.name: Faded pea green
pea.role: The stamp, larger headings, simple plant drawings.
pea.rule: Headings, the stamp and drawings only, at 56px or larger on a 1080px canvas (3.9:1 on cream passes for large text, not body). It's faded ink, so never pair it with a brighter green.

tomato.name: Tomato red
tomato.role: A box number, a sow-by date, a handwritten circle around one instruction.
tomato.rule: One red thing per post. Red means 'look here', and two of them cancel each other out. Large type (48px or more) or marks only (4.1:1 on cream).

avoid.reason: Green next to red reads as Christmas, not garden.
Cream text on a green fill turns the stamp into a button. Keep green as ink, not a fill.

material_notes: Kraft cardboard brings its own color. Don't recolor it to match the palette.
The green stamp prints a little darker on the box than on the insert. Keep that difference in photos; the hex above is the intended ink, not a correction to apply to photos.

wordmark.description: Chunky, closely spaced letters with slightly softened corners, like a rubber stamp used a few dozen times. Stacked HALF ACRE / CLUB so it fits a small seed envelope.
wordmark.rule: A little uneven ink at the edges, never distressing on every letter. One worn edge reads as real; a texture on everything reads as a filter. The stamp sketch says to try it without a border.

body.description: A plain sans serif with open shapes for everything people need to read.
body.rule: Instructions are the one place legibility beats charm. They should read like someone wrote them standing at the counter: 'Add water until the soil feels like a wrung-out sponge.'

hand.description: Handwriting for a date label or a correction on an early proof.
hand.rule: At most one handwritten element per post, a few words long. Occasional handwriting feels like somebody picked up a pen; constant handwriting feels like a font.

shape.rule: Slightly soft corners, slightly off-square stamps. Nothing perfectly round, nothing perfectly straight.
